title: The page forbids pinch-zoom for the whole page
body:
## Summary
The viewport meta sets maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no, which blocks zoom on every control, not only on the drawing pad.

## Description
companion/index.html:5. WCAG 1.4.4 (resize text). The pad already has touch-action:none (companion/index.html:34), which is what keeps a drawing gesture from zooming; the page-wide ban also stops a low-vision viewer from enlarging the 11-12 px status and labels. Removing it may let a stray double-tap zoom the nav, which is a product call.

## Flow
- a low-vision viewer pinches the status line
- nothing happens

## Expected impact
Readable status and labels for low-vision viewers; possible accidental zoom on the nav.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - text can be enlarged
Before: zoom blocked page-wide
After: unmeasurable as a benefit without users; the mechanical part is a one-line meta change
Method: simulation - the pad's touch-action already isolates the gesture; the trade-off is taste
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
companion/index.html:5 `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no, viewport-fit=cover">`
companion/index.html:34 `touch-action:none;` on #pad
escalation: direction - accessibility vs accidental zoom on a one-handed remote

title: All 25 pen controls are under the 44 px touch guideline

title: A worktree's desk/node_modules is a live junction into the operator's install
body:
## Summary
The preflight links desk/node_modules to the main checkout's install, so any recursive delete in a worktree can empty the operator's desk/node_modules.

## Description
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs ensure() links the whole directory (linkDir, a junction on Windows). The preflight itself only ever unlinks, but every tool downstream sees a real-looking directory: on 2026-10-08 a `git worktree remove --force` walked the junction and emptied the donor (memory: worktree-remove-wipes-donor-node-modules). The same link is why the missing .bin of the donor reached every worktree. Alternatives: npm ci into the worktree (slow, network), a per-worktree directory of per-package junctions plus its own .bin (no write into the donor, still shared packages), or a read-only copy. Each trades disk, time and isolation; the choice changes how every autopilot worktree is provisioned.

## Flow
- a worktree is provisioned by the preflight
- any recursive cleanup that follows reparse points runs in it
- the operator's desk/node_modules is emptied; the main checkout cannot run the desk or the gate

## Expected impact
The operator's install stops being one cleanup away from deletion. Cost: provisioning time or disk per worktree.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a worktree cannot destroy the operator's install
Before: 1 incident (2026-10-08); every worktree shares the donor install read-write through the link
After: unmeasured - depends on the provisioning chosen
Method: simulation - three walked cases: git worktree remove --force (happened), rm -rf desk in a worktree, an npm install run inside the linked directory
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence:
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs:94 linkDir: fs.symlinkSync(from, to, 'junction')
memory 2026-10-08: a --force remove emptied firetv/desk/node_modules

title: device-rules-test needs tools/node_modules, which the worktree preflight never links
body:
## Summary
Since the A/B drain moved the ink classifier into tools/device.mjs (05980d12) and the relay stub test opened ws clients (fd1f0b5e), desk's rules gate loads pngjs and ws from tools/node_modules; worktree-preflight links only desk/node_modules.

## Description
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs ensure() returns early once desk/node_modules is usable and never looks at tools/. In the sweep worktree device-rules-test went 11 red (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND pngjs, ws) until tools/node_modules was junctioned by hand; then 78 green. The main checkout has tools/ installed, so the operator's gate is green.

## Flow
- autopilot worktree, npm test -> pretest links desk/node_modules only -> device-rules-test imports device.mjs -> pngjs missing -> 11 red
- fix: preflight also links tools/node_modules from the same donor when absent, or device.mjs imports pngjs lazily inside the capture path

## Expected impact
Every autopilot worktree's npm test reads green again without a hand junction.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the gate runs in a worktree
Before: device-rules-test 11 of 11 red in a worktree without tools/node_modules
After: 0 red with tools/node_modules linked (measured by hand)
Method: probe - the hand junction is the fix's own shape
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'pngjs' imported from tools/device.mjs; Error: Cannot find module 'ws'
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs ensure(): if (usable(dest)) return { action: "present", dest };

title: Vision retries without think on any failed status, doubling 404/500 calls
instrument: stubbed fetch counting POSTs per status (404 model missing, 500, 400 think rejected) plus one recorded Ollama reply for think on a non-thinking model, to pin which status the retry is for
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts retries the request without `think` after any non-ok status, not only after the rejection the retry exists for.

## Description
vision.ts:48-49: `let res = await post({...body, think:false}); if (!res.ok) res = await post(body);`. A 404 for a model that is not pulled, or a 500, sends the whole image a second time and drops the first status and body. vision.ts:4 states the purpose: retry for models that reject the think key. Narrowing it needs the status Ollama actually returns for that rejection, which this round could not record (no live calls).

## Flow
- model not pulled -> 404 -> second POST with the full image -> 404 again, ~2x latency
- fix: retry only on the think-rejection status, keep the first error otherwise

## Expected impact
A missing vision model fails in one round trip instead of two. The risk is a wrong status guess, which would stop the think fallback from firing.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one request per failure that cannot be fixed by dropping think
Before: 2 POSTs on 404/500 (read from vision.ts:48-49)
After: 1 POST predicted
Method: simulation - three walked cases (404, 500, 400 think); probe needs a recorded Ollama reply
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts:48-49
desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts:4 "`think: false` first, retried without for models that reject the key"
note: held for owner: assumes Ollama 400 on rejected think

title: One engines suite process hung about 25 min under heavy load
instrument: the load23 harness (32 concurrent x N, 20 burners) with node --test-timeout and a SIGTERM handler that prints process._getActiveHandles(), to name the handle that held the process
body:
## Summary
In the Before measurement for case 23, 1 of 64 loaded runs of tools/engines-rules-test.cjs did not exit for about 25 minutes, after its tests had reported, and had to be killed.

## Description
The process (started 18:57:12) was still alive after the rest of the round ended. Its output had already reached case 23, which the harness parsed. Something kept the event loop alive. Candidates are the session store ticker cleared in after() (engines-rules-test.cjs:228), a pending stub timer, or the child spawned in case 7. run-rules would catch it only at the 600 s RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT, as a red suite.

## Flow
- load23: 32 x 2 runs beside 20 burners -> 63 exit, 1 alive at +25 min
- instrument: dump active handles on timeout

## Expected impact
If it recurs inside run-rules, it costs a 10-minute red. Naming the handle decides whether it is the suite or the machine.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every suite process exits after its last test
Before: 1 of 64 loaded runs hung (not reproduced in the 64-run After round)
After: unknown until the handle is named
Method: experiment - the same harness twice; the hang appeared once, so no deterministic rung yet
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: Lesson windows and queries are embedded with one role on an asymmetric model
body:
## Summary
lessons.ts embeds the transcript windows and the problem query through the same call with no role, while the default model (nomic-embed-text) is trained with search_document/search_query prefixes.

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:79 (windows) and :137 (query) both call embed({ texts, use: "lesson-window" }); desk/src/lib/engines/embed.ts:14 defaults OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL to nomic-embed-text. Registry technique retrieval/embedding-lifecycle, "The role is a fifth input": name the role at both call sites and put it in the stamp and any content-keyed cache - the cache digest (lessons.ts digestOf) and CACHE_VERSION would move with it. The model is env-configurable, so the prefix must be per model. Whether recall improves on these 8 lessons is the open figure.

## Flow
- the hint route picks a lesson and asks bestWindow for the nearest window to the problem
- today: query and windows share one role; the technique predicts quietly worse recall
- fix: document role on windows, query role on the problem, role in the digest

## Expected impact
The seek target inside a lesson may land closer to the method the problem needs. A cache rebuild once.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - seek-target recall
Before: no labelled set; recall unmeasured
After: needs a labelled problem -> window set run against local Ollama with and without prefixes
Method: simulation - the figure needs live embeddings from the operator Ollama; gates forbid live model calls, so neither this round nor a Lane B worker can take it
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:79 `await embed({ texts: w.map((x) => x.text), use: "lesson-window" })`
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:104 `await embed({ texts: [query], use: "lesson-window" })`
registry: knowledge/software-engineering/llm-agent/prompt-and-context/retrieval/techniques/embedding-lifecycle.md "The role is a fifth input"

title: The wrong-PIN limit is a lockout, which the pairing standard calls a DoS lever
body:
## Summary
device-pairing / timing-defenses prefers a fixed delay on every failed attempt over a lockout table, because a lockout keyed on attacker-suppliable input lets anyone lock out the legitimate holder; the pen's limit is a 5-strike, 30 s desk-wide lockout.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt PairingDesk.check locks every hello, the right PIN included, after MAX_WRONG_PINS. Since f0189837 that covers LAN connections too, so a LAN neighbour sending 5 wrong hellos every 30 s keeps the viewer from pairing indefinitely (before it, they could instead brute-force and take the pen, which is worse). The technique's answer is a fixed artificial delay before each refusal, applied uniformly, which a sans-IO core can express only as an effect the shell carries out (tv-app PenSessionHost). Parallel connections defeat a per-connection delay, so the real choice (delay, lockout, longer PIN, both) is a policy call.

## Flow
- a neighbour scripts 5 wrong hellos per 30 s
- the viewer's right PIN is refused "too many wrong PINs"
- the viewer cannot pair while the script runs

## Expected impact
Decides which attacker the pairing defends against best: the guesser (now limited) or the jammer (now enabled).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - neither guessing nor jamming the pairing is cheap
Before: jam: 5 hellos per 30 s keep pairing closed; guess: 5 per 30 s
After: unmeasurable until the policy is chosen (fixed delay needs a shell-side delay effect and a parallel-connection cap)
Method: simulation - walked through PairingDesk.check with an interleaved jammer; the rung above needs the shell change in tv-app
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
ai-registry device-pairing/techniques/timing-defenses.md "a lockout keyed on an attacker-suppliable identifier is a tool for locking out the legitimate holder"
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:68 PairingDesk.check `if (lockedUntilMs != null) return PinCheck.LOCKED`
escalation: direction - choose the throttle policy (lockout vs fixed delay vs PIN length); needs tv-app

After: 0 (predicted)

title: The TV credential never expires and cannot be revoked
body:
## Summary
The desk-tv cookie is HMAC(key,"tv"), lives 400 days, and the key never turns over, so any browser that once opened /tv?key= is the TV until pairing.json is deleted.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:122-124 tvToken = sign("tv"), a constant per key; COOKIE maxAge 400 days (:29); a reset forgets phones (forgetAllPhones) but never the TV; no list of TVs exists. The registry technique device-pairing/revocation-and-expiry: "minted credentials carry an absolute expiry ... no forever as the path of least resistance" and "a revoked credential fails its next presentation". Phones meet it (30-day lapse, cap 8, forget); the TV does not. Fix options for the owner: a key rotation on TV reset (every TV re-opens the printed address), or a TV list like the phones.

## Flow
- a visitor once opens the printed TV address on their laptop
- they are the TV, with the pin, for 400 days
- nothing on the desk can say "out" to that browser short of deleting pairing.json

## Expected impact
Decides whether the desk can withdraw a TV. A rotation forces every real TV to re-open the printed address, which is why the owner decides.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a TV grant that can end
Before: 0 ways to revoke a TV credential; no expiry beyond the cookie age
After: owner choice: rotation on reset, or a listed TV with the phones lapse rule
Method: simulation - the change alters the pairing model (what a TV is), an architecture call; no figure decides the product question
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:124 `export const tvToken = () => sign("tv");`
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:29 maxAge 400 days
registry: knowledge/software-engineering/security/identity-and-access/device-pairing/techniques/revocation-and-expiry.md "Expiry at every layer"

title: any LAN client can dial the relay as the TV and receive the phone's PIN
body:
## Summary
relay-stub listens on 0.0.0.0, gives the TV slot to whoever upgrades at /tv (closing the real TV), and ignores the session id RelayTransport documents (tools/relay-stub.mjs:76-82, 122; tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt:28-32).

## Description
RelayTransport says the relay "pairs one TV with one phone by session id" (wss://relay/tv?session=abc, phone at /?session=abc). The stub has one global TV slot and one pen slot. A second /tv dialer replaces the TV and is forwarded the phone's hello - PIN included - and every stroke. The PIN check stays on the TV by design, so the relay is exactly where TV identity must be decided, and nothing decides it. Fixing the stub alone is easy; the decision is the production relay's contract (session ids, who may claim the TV side), which is architecture.

## Flow
- relay-test (or a dev) runs the stub on 0.0.0.0:9787
- a LAN host connects ws://<host>:9787/tv
- the real TV is closed; the impostor receives the phone's {"type":"hello","pin":...}

## Expected impact
Today a dev-time exposure on the LAN; for the hosted relay it decides whether a stranger can take over a living-room session. Escalated: the relay contract is a product architecture call (docs/PLATFORM-RISK.md).

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the relay binds a TV side to one session
Before: TV identity checks in the stub: 0; session id honoured: no
After: not built - needs the contract decision
Method: simulation - architecture escalation; a stub-only patch would not settle the production relay
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
impact: Today a dev-time exposure on the LAN; for the hosted relay it decides whether a stranger can take over a living-room session. Escalated: the relay contract is a product architecture call (docs/PLATFORM-RISK.md).

title: Clip keeps playing after Home: the player has no lifecycle or audio focus
body:
## Summary
The ExoPlayer is built in a remember and released only when the composition is disposed (activity destroy); nothing pauses it on stop, and it does not request audio focus.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:168-176 builds the player with playWhenReady = true and REPEAT_MODE_ALL and releases it only in DisposableEffect.onDispose; Home on a Fire TV stops but does not destroy the activity, so a clip with audio keeps playing behind the launcher, looping. No setAudioAttributes(handleAudioFocus) either, so another app taking focus does not pause it. Registry: media-playback / media-resource-lifecycle - "audio that keeps playing after its surface is gone ... reapers for audible resources are bound to the owning scope's teardown"; a stopped activity is the interruption exit nobody tests.

## Flow
- play a clip -> press Home -> activity onStop, composition alive
- player still playing (REPEAT_MODE_ALL) with no surface
- fix: pause on ON_STOP (resume per the viewer's last state on ON_START), audio attributes with focus handling

## Expected impact
A viewer leaving the app no longer hears the clip from the home screen. Could break: a pen session expecting playback to continue in the background (none documented).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - playback stops with its surface
Before: simulation: 0 of 2 interruption exits handled (stop, focus loss); 1 of 3 exits (destroy) reaps the player
After: predicted 3 of 3; falsified if Fire OS destroys the activity on Home (then the before already stops)
Method: simulation - three exits walked in MainActivity.kt; a device is needed to observe audio after Home
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A viewer leaving the app no longer hears the clip from the home screen. Could break: a pen session expecting playback to continue in the background (none documented).
method: simulation - three exits walked in MainActivity.kt; a device is needed to observe audio after Home
instrument: device run on the Fire TV Stick: start the app, press Home, then `adb shell dumpsys media.audio_flinger` / `dumpsys audio` for an active track from dev.telestrator.tv and logcat of the 30 Hz loop position advancing; same run after the fix (pause in onStop or on Lifecycle.Event.ON_STOP, setAudioAttributes(..., handleAudioFocus = true)). Lane B because no emulator or device is available here.
ab_note: needs the Stick: dumpsys audio after Home

title: LanTransport says a bind failure never leaves start(); a probe says it does
body:
## Summary
The comment at LanTransport.kt:86-88 says Ktor's BindException does not come out of start() and only reaches the handler; on Ktor CIO 2.3.12 (JVM) it does both, so the handler writes the failure card during retries the loop is about to win.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt:86-88 (comment) vs LanTransport.kt:114-131 (retry branch that only works if start() throws). Probe this round (scratch JUnit test, not committed): port held by a ServerSocket, embeddedServer(CIO, parentCoroutineContext = handler).start(wait = false) -> start threw JobCancellationException whose cause chain holds java.net.BindException (isBindFailure() true), AND the handler received BindException. So the retry branch is live, and the handler sets `_failure` (LanTransport.kt:91) for a failure the loop retries; MainActivity's poll (MainActivity.kt:85-92) can paint the Failed card until a later attempt clears it. Device behaviour is unverified, and the comment records a crash fix on Fire OS, so the fix must not be landed blind: risk 4.

## Flow
- previous process still holds 8765 -> portIsFree passes in a race or fails later -> engine.start throws and the handler fires
- handler: _failure = port message -> poll shows Failed
- 300 ms later an attempt succeeds -> _failure = null

## Expected impact
Removes a red "port in use" flash during a normal relaunch, and a comment that would mislead the next person touching the crash fix. Could break: if Fire OS behaves as the comment says, ignoring bind failures in the handler would hide a real one - which is what the device run decides.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the comment and the failure path agree with the engine
Before: probe (JVM, Ktor CIO 2.3.12): start() threw with BindException in the chain, handler also fired; 2 writers of _failure for one bind failure
After: predicted 1 writer (the retry loop); untested on device
Method: experiment - a scratch JUnit probe on the desktop JVM; the Android runtime needs a device
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
PROBE chain=[JobCancellationException: LazyStandaloneCoroutine is cancelling, JobCancellationException ..., java.net.BindException: Address already in use: bind] isBind=true
handler=java.net.BindException: Address already in use: bind
LanTransport.kt:86 "Ktor binds inside its own accept coroutine, so a BindException does not come back out of start()"
impact: Removes a red "port in use" flash during a normal relaunch, and a comment that would mislead the next person touching the crash fix. Could break: if Fire OS behaves as the comment says, ignoring bind failures in the handler would hide a real one - which is what the device run decides.
method: experiment - a scratch JUnit probe on the desktop JVM; the Android runtime needs a device
instrument: the same probe on the Stick: hold port 8765 (adb shell toybox nc -l -p 8765 or a second build), launch, and record whether engine.start throws (with BindException in the chain) and whether the CoroutineExceptionHandler also fires; then the fix (handler ignores bind failures, the retry loop owns them; comment corrected) and the same run: the card must not show "port in use" while a later attempt succeeds.
ab_note: needs the Stick with port 8765 held

title: Link poll and frame loop keep running while the app is stopped
body:
## Summary
MainActivity's 1 Hz link poll enumerates network interfaces on the main thread and, like the 30 Hz frame loop, never stops when the activity is stopped.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:85-92 `lifecycleScope.launch { while (true) { ... transport.pairingUrl() ... delay(LINK_POLL_MS) } }` runs on Dispatchers.Main and calls LanTransport.lanAddress() (NetworkInterface.getNetworkInterfaces, tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt:148-155) once a second for the life of the activity, including after Home. The 30 Hz loop at MainActivity.kt:179-188 is a LaunchedEffect with delay(33), not frame-clock based, so it also keeps polling the player. Fire TV is a constrained device (TV, not a battery) - the cost is CPU and main-thread time shared with the pen path.

## Flow
- Home -> onStop
- poll keeps enumerating interfaces on Main at 1 Hz; frame loop keeps reading the player at 30 Hz
- fix: repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) for the poll; address read on Dispatchers.IO

## Expected impact
A backgrounded telestrator stops spending main-thread time. Could break: a pen session that relies on the poll while stopped (the server and heartbeat do not depend on it).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - zero background polling
Before: source count: 2 loops with no lifecycle bound; 1 NetworkInterface enumeration per second on Main
After: predicted 0 while stopped; falsified if Fire OS destroys the activity on Home
Method: simulation - loops enumerated in MainActivity.kt; timing needs a device
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A backgrounded telestrator stops spending main-thread time. Could break: a pen session that relies on the poll while stopped (the server and heartbeat do not depend on it).
method: simulation - loops enumerated in MainActivity.kt; timing needs a device
instrument: device run: press Home, wait 60 s, then `adb shell dumpsys cpuinfo` / `top -n 1 | grep telestrator` and a systrace of the main thread; same after moving both loops under repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) and the NetworkInterface read off Main.
ab_note: needs the Stick: CPU after Home

title: Pairing card and paired dot sit inside the TV overscan margin
body:
## Summary
PairingCard is inset 24 dp and the paired dot 20 dp from the top-right corner; Amazon's 5% safe zone is 48 dp x 27 dp at 1080p (960 x 540 dp).

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:104 `.padding(24.dp)` (Card) and PairingCard.kt:57 `.padding(20.dp)` (Chip), aligned TopEnd by tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:242-245 PairingCard(modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.TopEnd)). Fire TV design guidance keeps content 5% in from each edge for overscan; on a TV that overscans, the PIN digits and the QR's right quiet zone are the first to be cut. The repo states the same rule for its other TV surface (docs/DESIGN-ON-AIR.md:47 "5% safe zone"), though On Air itself governs Study Desk, not the telestrator.

## Flow
- TV with 5% overscan -> outer 96 px cropped
- card right edge at 48 px from the edge -> the right 48 px of the card cropped, QR quiet zone lost

## Expected impact
The QR stays scannable and the PIN readable on overscanning TVs. Could break: the card sits further into the picture by 24 dp.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - pairing furniture inside the safe zone
Before: 3 of 3 corner elements (card, dot, status line at 0 dp) outside the 48 x 27 dp margin
After: predicted 0 of 3; falsified if the Stick reports a density where 24 dp >= 5% (it does not at 1080p/xhdpi)
Method: simulation - the stated rule checked against the dp constants; pixels need a screencap
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
PairingCard.kt:57 .padding(20.dp)  (Chip)
PairingCard.kt:104 .padding(24.dp) (Card)
MainActivity.kt:257 status Text .align(Alignment.BottomStart) with no outer padding
impact: The QR stays scannable and the PIN readable on overscanning TVs. Could break: the card sits further into the picture by 24 dp.
method: simulation - the stated rule checked against the dp constants; pixels need a screencap
instrument: adb screencap on the Stick at 1920x1080 with the invite up and with a pen paired: measure the card's right/top edge and the dot's offset in px; the rule is >= 96 px horizontal and >= 54 px vertical (5% per side). Same capture after padding(horizontal = 48.dp, vertical = 27.dp).

title: The paired state is a 16 dp green dot with no semantics
body:
## Summary
LinkView.Chip renders a bare Box with a green background and no contentDescription, so the paired state is colour-only and silent to a screen reader.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:55-61: Box(...).size(16.dp).background(Color(0xFF2ECC71)...).testTag("pairedChip"). ## Flow
- phone pairs -> LinkView.Chip -> green dot
- VoiceView: nothing to announce
- fix: add link_paired string and a semantics contentDescription

## Expected impact
A low-vision viewer can tell a pen is connected. Could break: nothing visible.

After: predicted 6 of 6

Result: better

title: The pointer ring is 5 px at any image size, against point.py's own warning
body:
## Summary
vision/point.py mark() draws a fixed 5 px ring whatever the frame width, though its docstring says a ring thin enough to vanish in the model's downscale is worse than none.

## Description
vision/point.py mark loops range(5) for thickness while the radius scales with width (radius_frac * w). poc_ocr runs at PHOTO_W 1280 (5 px = 0.39% of width), but point.py's CLI takes any frame: a 4032 px phone photo gets 0.12%, about 1 px after a downscale to ~1000 px. Proposed: thickness proportional to width with a floor (e.g. max(5, w // 256)). Whether the thin ring actually loses the model is a model question; the product's selection no longer uses a ring (nearestItem), so the risk is the lab's own pointer evidence.

## Flow
- python vision/point.py --frame <4032 px photo> --at x,y --ask ... --compare
- predicted: the ring is ~1 px after downscale; the model answers about something else
- falsified if the 4032 px run selects as well as the 1280 px one

## Expected impact
The lab's pointer evidence holds on real phone photos. Could break: a thicker ring hides a neighbouring item's text.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the ring survives downscale
Before: thickness 5 px absolute: 0.39% of 1280 px, 0.12% of 4032 px
After: proportional thickness (predicted: hits unchanged at 1280, better at 4032)
Method: simulation - the figure that matters (hits) needs live model runs, which no gate may make
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: vision/point.py mark(): r = radius_frac * w; for i in range(5): d.ellipse(...); docstring "Thickness is not cosmetic"
instrument: operator-only: poc_ocr circle_test on the maths page rendered 4032 px wide, fixed 5 px vs proportional ring, hits out of 4 at mild and harsh
